conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim that regular vitamin C prevents colds is largely false for the general population, citing high-quality Cochrane reviews showing no effect on cold incidence.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
## The evidence does not support "yes" for the general population

The premise needs correction: for most people, regular vitamin C intake does **not** prevent colds. The Cochrane systematic review (29 trials, over 11,000 participants) found that regular vitamin C supplementation in the general community had essentially no effect on cold incidence—pooled risk ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.94–1.00), a negligible and barely significant reduction ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23440782/)). NCBI's patient-oriented summary confirms: "it wasn't possible to prevent colds by taking vitamin C every day over a longer period of time," though duration was shortened by about 10% ([NCBI Bookshelf](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279544/)).

**There is one notable exception**: in people under acute physical or cold-environmental stress—marathon runners, skiers, soldiers in subarctic conditions—regular vitamin C supplementation (≥0.2 g/day) cut cold incidence by about 50% across five trials with 598 participants ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23440782/)). This effect has not been replicated in ordinary community populations.

For everyone else, benefits are limited to modestly reducing the **duration and severity** of colds once they occur—roughly 8–14% shorter duration, and up to 15% less severe with doses ≥1 g/day—not preventing them from happening ([PMC, Vitamin C for the common cold and pneumonia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39803741/)).

**Conclusion**: The claim that regular vitamin C prevents colds is largely false for the general population, based on the highest-quality evidence (Cochrane reviews). It appears true only for a narrow subgroup under extreme physical/environmental stress. The answer should be "no, with an exception," not simply "yes."
